sources.title: NGSS MS-LS3-2: Develop and use a model to describe why asexual reproduction results in offspring with identical genetic information and sexual reproduction results in offspring with genetic variation
OpenStax Biology 2e, 24.1 Characteristics of Fungi (yeast budding)
OpenStax Biology 2e, 27.1 Features of the Animal Kingdom (budding)

steps.title: Bacterium
steps.instruction: Trace the bacterium at the top left.

note.text: Bacteria reproduce by binary fission: one cell splits into two.
A bacterium has one loop-shaped chromosome.
The cell copies its DNA and grows longer.

steps.title: Two copies
steps.instruction: Draw the two copies of the DNA.

note.text: Each copy is exact, so each new cell gets the same instructions.
A new wall forms across the middle and the cell splits into two identical daughter cells.
Yeast is a single-celled fungus. It reproduces by budding.

steps.title: Bud
steps.instruction: Trace the yeast cell with a bud bulging out.

note.text: A bulge forms on the side of the cell. The nucleus divides, and one copy moves into the bud.

steps.title: New cell
steps.instruction: Trace the parent and the bud that broke off.

note.text: The bud detaches as a new yeast cell.

steps.title: Steps
steps.instruction: Draw the arrows between the steps.

note.text: Each arrow is one step in time. Both processes need just one parent.

steps.title: Identical
steps.instruction: Compare the offspring with the parent.
steps.question: How do the offspring's genes compare with the parent's?

options.text: They're identical, because there's only one parent and its DNA is copied
options.feedback: Yes. Asexual reproduction makes genetically identical offspring, unless a rare mutation happens.

options.text: Half from each of two parents
options.feedback: That's sexual reproduction. Here there's only one parent.
The DNA is copied, so the offspring match the parent.
Every cell needs DNA. The offspring get an exact copy.

steps.title: Trade-off
steps.question: A new disease kills one strain of bacteria. Why might a whole colony made by fission die?

options.text: They're all identical, so if one can't survive it, none can
options.feedback: Right. Sexual reproduction makes varied offspring, so some may survive a change. Identical ones can't.
The cells are healthy. The problem is that they're all the same.
They can. And identical cells all share the same weakness.
Fission is fast. The risk is that every cell is identical.
